q: Why does each reduced FAD yield fewer ATP (~1.5) than each reduced NAD (~2.5)?
options: FADH2 carries only one electron, while NADH carries four electrons to the chain
FADH2 passes electrons in later (via complex II), bypassing the first proton pump
FADH2 donates its electrons straight to O2 without passing through the carriers
FADH2 is made in the cytoplasm and must use ATP to be moved into the mitochondrion
explanation: NADH donates electrons to complex I, which pumps protons. FADH2, held within succinate dehydrogenase (complex II), feeds its electrons to ubiquinone without pumping any. Fewer protons pumped per electron pair means a smaller contribution to the gradient and fewer ATP made by ATP synthase. Both carriers deliver 2 electrons.
